Why This Is Asked
Tests integration of image provenance with runtime attestation in a multi-tenant CNF environment, plus policy automation and rollback

## Key Concepts
- Image provenance (Cosign + SBOM)
- Runtime attestation (TPM/measured boot)
- Kubernetes admission controls (Kyverno/OPA)
- Per-tenant isolation and testability
- Canary rollout and rollback

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign and attest
cosign sign -key kms-key.pem docker.io/org/cnf:tag
cosign attest docker.io/org/cnf:tag --attestation-file attestation.yaml
```
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cnf-provenance-runtime
spec:
  rules:
  - name: attest-and-sbom-check
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must carry cnf.io/attested and cnf.io/sbom annotations"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            metadata:
              annotations:
                cnf.io/attested: "?*"
                cnf.io/sbom: "?*"
```

- How would you test attestation failure paths and rollbacks?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests design of scalable edge enforcement using in-kernel routing (eBPF) and Kubernetes operators, a realistic CNF ops pattern across regions.

## Key Concepts
- CustomResourceDefinition design for per-tenant network policy
- Kubernetes controller reconciliation to reflect CRD state into eBPF maps
- Sidecar-based map loading and hot-reload without downtime
- Rollout strategies, observability, and fault-tolerance

## Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: TenantNetworkPolicy
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantnetworkpolicies.example.net
spec:
  group: example.net
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              rateLimit:
                type: integer
              allowedCIDR:
                type: string
              blockedPorts:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: integer
```
```yaml
# Tenant example (t8)
apiVersion: example.net/v1
kind: TenantNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: t8
spec:
  tenantID: t8
  rateLimit: 100
  allowedCIDR: 10.1.0.0/16
  blockedPorts: [22]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you audit per-tenant policy changes with minimal performance impact?
- How would you handle conflicting policies from multiple controllers or regions?
- What are the failure modes during map reloads and how do you mitigate them?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime attestation bridging CI and runtime, using SPIFFE/mTLS, OPA, and per-tenant revocation. Evaluates trade-offs around performance, key management, and revocation latency.

## Key Concepts

- Runtime attestation evidence (image digest, SBOM hash, runtime state)
- Attestation service with mutual TLS and SPIFFE identities
- Admission control with OPA to gate scheduling
- Per-tenant revocation and key rotation for attestations
- Testing in a single namespace before broader rollout

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: attestation-agent
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: example/attestation-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: ATTESTATION_ENDPOINT
          value: https://attestor.default.svc.cluster.local
        - name: CERT_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.crt
        - name: KEY_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.key
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you scale attestation for thousands of CNFs without adding startup latency?
- How would you handle revocation propagation when an attacker signs a new image at runtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical knowledge of policy-as-code and admission control in a CNF context. It requires understanding of per-tenant isolation, Rego policy design, and webhook integration without relying on image signing.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes admission webhooks
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) and Rego
- Per-tenant policy isolation via ConfigMaps
- Namespace-scoped testing manifests and observability

## Code Example
```rego
package k8s.cnf.constraints
default allow = false

# Example policy loaded per-namespace
allow {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.metadata.namespace == z
  z := data.{namespace}.allowedNodes
  input.spec.nodeName == allowed_node
  allowed_node == "worker-1"
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  policy.rego: |
    package k8s.cnf.constraints
    default allow = false
    allow {
      input.kind == "Pod"
      input.metadata.namespace == "tenant-a"
      input.spec.nodeName == "worker-1"
    }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy updates without disrupting tenants?
- What are trade-offs of per-namespace policies versus a centralized policy store?

```yaml
kind: CNFProvenance
metadata:
  name: tenant-a_cnf_provenance
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroup: apps
        kinds: [Deployment]
  parameters:
    requireSignature: true
    requireSBOM: true
    tenantMatcher: '^tenant-a-.*$'
```
